historical_references.reference: Mostakim was a title of the Hindu king of Magadha, in what is now eastern India, during the 5th century BCE. The title Mostakim is derived from the Sanskrit word 'mostaka', meaning 'beloved of Indra'. Indra was an important deity in the Vedic religion, which was the dominant religion of the Magadhan people during that time.

historical_references.reference: Mostakim is also mentioned in the Hindu epic Mahabharata as the name of a famous charioteer of the prince Bhima. He was said to be the son of the celestial being Sahasrarjaya and the river Saraswati. The name Mostakim is not explicitly stated to be derived from any specific deity in this context, but it is mentioned that Mostakim was a name given to him by the sage Vyasa.
